origin: cwe/121/c Key Principles: fgets closes the overflow and leaves truncation behind; peek the next character to detect it

finding.name: Stack-based Buffer Overflow
finding.summary: gets(line) has no size limit and can write past the end of the 64-byte line stack array for any input longer than 63 characters.

trap: Replacing gets(line) with fgets(line, sizeof(line), stdin) closes the overflow but is an incomplete fix on its own: fgets splits an over-long line silently, leaving the remainder queued on stdin to be read as the start of the next call to read_command_line. A missing trailing newline in line does not by itself prove truncation - it can also mean the input ended exactly at line's capacity with only the newline left unread. The fix must also detect truncation and drain the rest of the line: after fgets succeeds, peek the next character with getchar() - EOF or '\n' means the line ended there; anything else means input is still queued, so drain to the next newline and reject the over-long line instead of silently processing only its first 63 characters.
must_preserve: For an input line that fits within line's capacity, read_command_line still copies it into out (bounded by out_capacity) and returns 0. An input line too long for line is rejected (returns -1), and no leftover bytes from a rejected line are left queued to corrupt the next call's read.
